caption:
Not at all what we expexted 😭

This is your sign to plan the hike better than us. We checked AllTrails and people said we’ll be fine. We are fine, but it was scary at one point 🫣 

It started with a chill forest trail to the famous Lake Sorapis.

🥾 But there are two main routes to the lake. Most people take the lower trail, which is easier and includes a few cable-assisted sections. It’s the more popular option and suitable for most hikers. 

There is also a Forcella Marcoira route - the one we took and it challenged us!

Normal route goes at the bottom of the mountain, while Forcella Marcoira is at the very top.

893 total elevation, most of which is gained on a few extremely steep sections.

Expect loose gravel, areas exposed to sun, and incredible panoramic views over the Dolomites. Only attempt this one if you’re properly equipped and comfortable with challenging hikes.

Also, use only the most used parts of the path.

caption:
The longest line in the Dolomites 😩

😅 If you have seen any photos of the Dolomites, you have probably seen someone standing on this exact narrow ridge at Cadini di Misurina.

🧗‍♀️ The reason there is always a queue here is that the final spur is extremely narrow with huge drops on both sides. Only one or two people can safely stand at the end at a time, so you literally have to take turns to take pictures.

⏰ We arrived at sunset, and the wait wasn’t too bad ~15 mins. Absolutely worth it. BUT! Some people say it can get up to an HOUR wait ⏰🤯

🥾 The hike itself is quite short with a steep section. It starts right from the same parking lot as Tre Cime, so it is really easy to add to your day if you are already in the area.

⛰️ If you don’t want to wait for a long time, there is a second viewpoint, slightly higher than the most popular one! Usually no wait or 5 mins wait.

The Dolomites - our UNESCO World Heritage Site, a place of silence, grandeur and untouched nature. But today, those who think of the once lonely peaks and clear mountain lakes often see a completely different picture: an ant invasion of tourists that rolls through the valleys in endless columns and occupies the peaks.
The biggest problem with this? Many of these visitors lack any reference or respect to the mountains. Our homeland is no longer valued, it is consumed. It is no longer about the experience of climbing or the tranquility of nature, but about the perfect photo.
We don't need influencers to artificially stage our mountains just to generate clicks and attract even more people from all over the world to roll over our sensitive mountain world.

caption:
Follow along if you’re planning a Dolomites trip this summer or next season 🇮🇹

🌼 First place - Alpe di Siusi (Seiser Alm)

🚗 Arrive before 9:00 a.m. if you’re driving. The road closes to private vehicles from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., although you can leave anytime.

🅿️ Parking costs €30 

📍 The famous viewpoint is about a 30-minute walk along the main asphalt road from the parking area. 

🌅 Sunset is the most magical time to visit, but sunrise and midday are beautiful too.

🌲 Adolf Munkel Trail & Geisler Alm

🚗 We arrived around 2:00 p.m. and luckily found parking.

🥾 The hike to Geisler Alm takes about 2 hours through a mostly shaded forest with moderate elevation.

COMMENT “Trail” to create an AllTrails aaclunt for FREE before you go. 

🍽️ Most mountain huts (including thos one) stop serving 
food around 5:00–6:00 p.m., so don’t arrive too late.

💧 There’s also a free water fountain outside to refill your bottles.

📸 Before heading back, stop by the famous wooden bench overlooking Geisler Alm and the Odle peaks. We stayed for sunset, and even with some clouds, it was one of our favorite evenings in the Dolomites.

🌊 Elora Gorge Tubing — Complete Guide 2026

📍 Location
• Just 1.5 hours from Toronto in Elora, Ontario
• A 2 km tubing ride through limestone cliffs and rapids on the Grand River

⏳ Season & Hours
• Open daily from Mid June – Labour Day (September 30)
• Weekends only until September 30 (weather permitting)
• Rentals close at 4 PM, equipment must be returned by 7 PM

🎟 Tickets & Pricing
• Online booking required (day-use passes often sell out)
• Park entry: $9/adult
• Tubing package: $54/person (tube, helmet, life jacket included)
• Refundable deposit: $75 per rental

🚗 Parking & Logistics
• Large parking lot inside Elora Gorge Conservation Area
• 1.3 km walk between launch point & exit (each way)
• No lifeguards on site — strong swimming skills recommended

🎒 What to Bring
• Closed-toe water shoes or running shoes with grip
• Waterproof phone case + strap (phones often get lost!)
• Sunglasses with strap, sunscreen, water, snacks
• Towel & change of clothes

🛟 Equipment
• No need to bring your own tube — rentals cover everything you need
• Helmets & lifejackets are mandatory (provided with rental)

✨ Tubing at Elora Gorge is one of the best summer adventures in Ontario!

Here’s what to know before doing Little Beehive after a Moraine Lake sunrise 👇

🥱 If you’re doing Alpine Start at Moraine Lake, expect to wake up around 2 AM and stay active the whole day, we were honestly exhausted by the time we started this hike (GO TO BED EARLY)

🥗 We stopped at Fairmont Lake Louise for a quick breakfast, one of the few decent options around, and the pre made salad we got was actually really good, just note that public washrooms are only at the parking lot

🥾 The hike to Lake Agnes Tea House is about 3.5 km one way with a steady uphill through the forest, pretty manageable but you’ll feel it

🌄 From there you can choose, Little Beehive is about 800 m further and easier, while Big Beehive adds around 1.5 km and is more challenging

💧 On the way you pass Mirror Lake and small waterfalls, which makes the whole hike feel way more interesting

🍵 The Tea House is a great stop for snacks and a break with really nice views over the lake

🎒 Pack light but bring essentials like water, snacks, and mosquito spray, you’ll need it

👟 Wear proper shoes because some parts of the trail are rocky and can get slippery

🐴 We saw people doing horseback rides here but honestly wouldn’t recommend it, the horses looked like they were struggling on the steeper sections

📸 If you want less crowded photos at Lake Louise, step onto the shallow rocks near the shore if your shoes allow

😵‍💫 By the end of this we had been awake for about 13 hours and decided to skip Big Beehive and head back

We wouldn’t recommend combining Moraine Lake sunrise and this hike in one day unless you’re really prepared

🚗 Land in Calgary and pick up your rental car
We went with Commune Auto, pricing depends on how much you drive, and then headed straight to Canmore which is about 1.5 hours away with amazing views the whole way

🏔️ Plan your arrival with sunset in mind
In late June the sun sets around 10pm, so you still have time to stop at spots like the Three Sisters viewpoint on your way

🏡 Stay in Canmore instead of Banff
It’s calmer, more affordable, and still super close to all the main spots

🍽️ Spend some time in Downtown Canmore
Walk around, grab food, check out local shops, and don’t miss the Bow River bridge

💸 Expect around 90 dollars per person per night for accommodation

🛒 Grab groceries for the next day
It makes early starts way easier and saves money

Starting your trip like this just makes everything feel more relaxed from day one 🌄

🚗 Drive the Icefields Parkway 
One of the most scenic drives in Canada and a must do 

❄️ Stop at Crowfoot Glacier 
Quick but impressive stop right off the road 

💧 Visit Bow Lake 
Super clear water and a really peaceful atmosphere 

📍 End at Peyto Lake 
Our favorite stop, the color of the lake is unreal 

👀 Skip the main viewpoint crowds 
It gets very busy, especially mid day 

🌲 Walk a bit further for a better view 
We found a quieter spot about 300m into the forest and it was even better

Here’s how to plan your visit so it actually goes smoothly 👇 

🚐 Book your shuttle in advance 
You can’t drive to Moraine Lake, so book through Parks Canada early 
Tickets sell out months ahead 

🌅 Go for the earliest time 
We took the 4 AM Alpine Start shuttle and it was 100% worth it 

📵 Download everything 
There’s no service at the parking lot, so screenshot your booking and maps 

🎟️ Keep your return ticket 
You’ll get a purple ticket from the driver for your shuttle back 

🥶 Be ready for the cold 
Before sunrise it’s freezing, bring layers, snacks, and something warm to drink 

⏳ Expect to wait a bit 
You’ll likely wait around an hour before sunrise, but the views are worth it 

🌄 Enjoy the quiet views 
Early morning means fewer people, calm water, and that unreal sunrise light 

🚶 Walk around the lake 
Easy trails with different viewpoints, super worth taking your time 

🛶 Canoe if you want the full experience 
Around 160 dollars per hour or bring your own paddleboard 

🏨 Stay nearby if you can 
There’s a lodge right there, but it books out far in advance 

➡️ Combine with Lake Louise 
Since you’re already there, it makes sense to visit both in one day

Comment “CRUISE” for more info and a 20% discount code for City Cruises 🚢

This makes for such a fun day trip from Ottawa (about 2 hours) or a weekend escape from Toronto (about 3 hours).

1️⃣ Almonte

🏘️ One of the cutest small towns we’ve visited in Ontario. Beautiful heritage buildings, a charming main street, and plenty of small-town character.

🚗 On the way, stop by Carleton Place and keep an eye out for the horse farm near Highway 29 & Pleasant Lane 🐴

2️⃣ 1000 Islands Cruise by @citycruisescanada 

🚢 The must-do experience in the region.

🏰 We cruised past Boldt Castle, Millionaire’s Row, Zavikon Island, and the Thousand Islands Bridge while taking in one of the most unique landscapes we’ve seen in Ontario.

☀️ Grab a spot on the open-air upper deck and enjoy the views.

3️⃣ 1000 Islands Tower

🌉 For about $20 CAD, you’ll get incredible 360° views over the islands, the St. Lawrence River, and both Canada and the USA.

📸 Easily one of the best viewpoints in the area.

4️⃣ Brockville

🚇 Don’t miss the Brockville Railway Tunnel. The combination of lights, music, and the historic tunnel makes it a truly unique experience.

🍜 We also stopped at Pho Hut for dinner before heading home.

Definitely one of our favorite Ontario road trips so far ❤️

Here are some spots around Niagara Falls that are 100% worth adding to your itinerary 👇

📍 Whirlpool Jet Boat Tours
Amazing, high-adrenaline experience like nothing we’ve tried before

📍 Niagara-on-the-Lake
Gorgeous Bridgerton-style town

📍 Niagara Floral Clock
Just a beautiful flower setup

📍 Floral Showhouse
Gorgeous flowers when everything is blooming and amazing magnolia and cherry blossoms nearby

📍 Buddhist Temple of Canada
Very interesting building that you wouldn’t expect to find here

📍 Falls Incline Railway
Stunning spot to observe the falls

📍 Queen Victoria Park
Great place to observe the falls and just relax near the flowers

📍 Centennial Lilac Garden
There aren’t many lilac gardens out there and this one is very beautiful

📍 Whirlpool Aero Car
A unique experience that on a sunny day looks stunning as you ride over the Niagara

📍 Fallsview Mall
Good quick stop if you need food or a break from walking

📍 Niagara Parks Botanical Gardens
One of the best places for a quiet walk, especially in spring

📍 Clifton Hill & Falls Avenue
Very touristy but fun if you want that classic Niagara vibe

📍 Skylon Tower
Best panoramic views over the falls and the whole area

📍 Queen Victoria Place
Nice viewpoint area that’s easy to stop by while walking

📍 Brock’s Monument
The whole park is worth visiting and the monument itself is huge and impressive

📍 Niagara City Cruises
Definitely a must, you get incredibly close to the falls and it’s such a memorable experience

caption:
🏔️Follow @across_continentss for the 7 day series

After landing in Venice and picking up our rental car, we started the drive toward the Dolomites.
And almost immediately made our first mistake 😅

🚗 We skipped the toll road to save about €10.
On paper, the scenic route looked only slightly longer. In reality, it added a lot more driving than expected, with endless towns, roundabouts, lower speed limits, and constant stops.
Pay the toll. Trust us, it’s worth it.

💙 Our first stop was Lago di Carezza, and it was the perfect introduction to the Dolomites.
Even with cloudy weather, the lake looked incredible. The water shifts between emerald and turquoise depending on the light, and the surrounding pine forest makes it feel straight out of a postcard.
📸 There are plenty of viewpoints around the lake and an easy walking trail that circles part of the shoreline.
🚗 Parking is located right beside the lake and costs around €10.

🛒 Before heading to our accommodation, we stopped in Bolzano to stock up on groceries.
Most supermarkets in smaller Dolomites towns close early, often around 7 or 8 p.m., so don’t leave shopping until the evening.

🏡 First 3 nights we stayed in the small village of Villandro (Leishof airbnb) which was high up on the hill.
Even though we liked it, and the host was very pleasant, the commute takes a while.
We suggest booking a hotel in Ortisei in advance for the best location in Western Dolomites.

🚘 We also rented a manual car and saved a few hundred dollars compared to an automatic. If you’re comfortable driving stick, it’s definitely worth considering.

Follow along if you’re planning a Dolomites trip this summer or next season 🇮🇹

🎲 5 GAMES & RULES EXPLAINED ⬇️

Send this to a friend you want to try these with 🍣😅

Before we dive in, follow @across_continentss for more fun date ideas and travel in Canada ✈️

We recently turned sushi date night into game night and honestly had way too much fun with these 😂

♟️ Sushi Checkers
You’ll need a board, parchment paper, a marker, plastic wrap, and sushi. Draw your checkerboard on the parchment paper and cover it with plastic wrap before placing the sushi. If you’re drawing directly on the surface, make sure to use food safe materials. Then just play regular checkers, but your pieces are sushi 🍣

😮 Chubby Bunny Sushi Edition
A classic challenge, but with sushi. We ordered sushi from @sushi96.ca and only managed to put two pieces in our mouths because their rolls are HUGE 😂 

Their sushi was fresh, delicious, and there were so many options to choose from. They even have dessert rolls like Tropical Paradise with kiwi, banana, and strawberry, plus viral favorites like the Dubai Roll and Nutella Roll 🍓🍫

🎁 Use code “ACROSS10” for 10% off your order

⭕❌ Sushi Tic Tac Toe
You’ll need a board, four sushi sticks, and sushi. Lay the sticks into a tic tac toe grid and play as usual. Simple, but surprisingly competitive 😆

🌶️ Wasabi Challenge
You’ll need sushi, wasabi, and either a mask or a partner willing to close their eyes. Secretly place wasabi under some sushi pieces while your partner isn’t looking. Take turns picking sushi and hope you don’t get the spicy surprise 😅

🚢 Sushi Battleship
You’ll need a divider, two sheets of paper, markers, and sushi. We used a 3x4 grid with letters for columns and numbers for rows. Hide your sushi locations, call coordinates, and see who finds their opponent’s sushi first 😎

caption:
🌸Follow @across_continentss for more Canada travel ideas like this⬇️

Here’s how we’d plan a perfect May day around Niagara Falls when everything starts blooming 👇 

🌸 Start at Niagara Parks Botanical Gardens 
One of the best spots for cherry blossoms, plus quiet paths and way fewer crowds than the falls

🌸 Walk the Niagara Parkway 
On the way toward Niagara-on-the-Lake you’ll find blooming trees scattered along the drive 

🌸 Stop near the Falls viewpoints 
There are small garden areas near Horseshoe Falls where you can catch blossoms with the falls in the background 

🌸 Head up the Skylon Tower 
Best panoramic views of the falls and the surrounding area, especially on a clear spring day 

⚡ Try the zipline over the falls 
If the weather is warm enough, this is one of the craziest ways to see Niagara

Comment “SALSA” for our full MEXICO Yucatán Peninsula guide with all the spots, tips & hidden gems 🇲🇽

Save this for your next trip 🇲🇽 

🌊 Diving at MUSA + Manchones Reef 
Diving here was honestly one of the most unique experiences we had in Mexico. It’s an underwater museum filled with statues, surrounded by coral reefs and marine life 🐠 

We went with @emiliodivecenter_1984 and everything went great!

🤿 Beginner vs certified divers 
If it’s your first time, they’ll teach you the basics on the beach before heading out. It’s also more expensive for non-certified divers, so getting certified beforehand makes everything way more relaxed and enjoyable. 

🚤 Getting there 
You’ll take about a 20-minute boat ride to the dive spots. Not gonna lie, the waves were pretty rough when we went and we felt it 😅 definitely bring seasickness pills just in case. 

🐢 What the dives are like 
You usually get 2 dives of around 30 minutes each. Swimming around the statues feels unreal, and the reef is full of marine life. 

🧴 What to bring 
Reef-safe sunscreen is a must, and wetsuits are included but we’d definitely recommend wearing one to stay warm. 

👥 Group vs private 
We went with a group, so timing depends on everyone. You can book private if you want more flexibility, but it’ll cost more. 

It’s one of those experiences that just feels completely different from anything else you’ll do in Mexico 🌊

caption:
I BET TOU DIDN’T KNOW ABOUT TIP 8 🇲🇽

Before we dive in, save this for your next trip and comment “SALSA” for a full Mexico Yucatán guide, which includes Cancun, Isla Mujeres, Playa del Carmen, Tulum, Valladolid, Chichén Itzá, cenotes, beaches, restaurants, and hidden gems 🇲🇽

Here are mistakes we’ve made (or seen) that can seriously impact your experience 👇

📍 Not paying Visitax
A required tourist tax in Quintana Roo that many people forget about.

📍 Not checking seaweed conditions
Sargassum can affect beach days. It’s worth checking before you plan.

📍 Not having offline maps downloaded
Signal can be unreliable. Google Maps offline saved us more than once.

📍 Not getting scuba certified before MUSA
You’ll save time, avoid stress, and enjoy the underwater museum way more.

📍 Forgetting seasickness pills
Boat rides, especially to MUSA, can get rough. The boat was shaking a lot, and we gor sick very fast 🫣

📍 Using money exchange instead of ATMs
ATMs usually give much better rates (the ones you see in Google) and cards like Wise might waive ATM fees up to some amount.

📍 Not booking a private airport transfer
After a long flight, this makes everything smoother, FASTER and less stressful.

📍 Not learning basic Spanish
Even a little Duolingo goes a long way. It helped us so many times in restaurants, parking lots and casual conversations.

📍 Not renting a bike in Tulum
Taxis can be insanely overpriced in the high season. Bikes are the easiest way to get around.

📍 Being afraid of spicy food
Most places can adjust spice levels, so don’t miss out on unique local dishes because of that.

📍 Not trying local fruits
We skipped fresh mango and pineapple at markets and still regret it 🥲

caption:
OUR TOP MEXICO FOOD ADVICES 🌮

Before we dive in — save this for your next trip 🇲🇽

Food is one of the best parts of traveling in Mexico, but there are a few things that can make your experience even better 👇

📍 DON’T ONLY RELY on hotel restaurants
Some of the best food in Mexico comes from small local spots and street stands.

📍 Not trying street food
Tacos, quesadillas, elotes, fresh juices -  street food is a huge part of Mexican culture and often the most authentic option.

📍 Skipping local markets
Markets are the best place to try traditional dishes, fresh fruit, and regional specialties.

📍 Not carrying cash
Many small restaurants and food stands are cash only, so having pesos with you is essential.

📍 Being afraid of spicy food
Salsas can be spicy, but most places let you decide the spiciness level. Start small and find your favorite.

📍 Ignoring local specialties
Every region has its own dishes - trying local food is part of the travel experience.

Mexican food is one of the highlights of visiting the country — explore beyond the tourist spots and you’ll find some incredible meals 🌮

caption:
❄️ WHO’S TUBING WITH YOU? 😎

But first — follow @across_continentss for more winter adventures, cozy date ideas, and hidden gems across Ontario! 🤍

If you’re not into skiing but still want to enjoy the slopes — snow tubing is your go-to winter thrill. Fast, easy, and absolutely hilarious (especially when you go down as a group 😅).

Here are the best tubing hills near Toronto 👇🏼

🛟 Snow Valley (Barrie) — One of the biggest tubing parks in Ontario! 14 chutes, 10-storey high, and a magic carpet lift back to the top.
🎟️ Tickets: from ~$35, book online early (they sell out fast!).

🛟 Lakeridge Resort (Uxbridge) — Closer to the city and great for families or beginners. They have 5 tubing lanes and warming areas to grab hot chocolate after.

🛟 Horseshoe Resort (Barrie) — Huge tubing hill with night lights and music — feels like a winter festival. You can also bundle it with spa access or dining for the perfect weekend getaway.

🛟 Chicopee Tube Park (Kitchener) — A bit of a drive, but super organized with fast lanes and great staff. Bonus: an indoor lounge to warm up between rides.

💡 Tips before you go:
• Dress in layers and bring waterproof gloves 🧤
• Book online (especially weekends)
• Bring a stick/tripod to attach to your phone/camera
• Night tubing must be fun with lights & music (we haven’t tried though)

It’s honestly one of the easiest and most fun things to do in Toronto this winter — no skills needed, just laughter and snow! ☃️

We’d been saving spa ideas for months and finally decided to start with Ste. Anne’s Spa @steannesspa, which is just 1,5 hrs from Toronto.

🍓Finding champagne, strawberries, and a gift set waiting for us in the room was such a lovely surprise, and we later found out that you can book this exact kind of experience as part of their Couples Package (which runs until the end of March)

🎟️ Ste. Annes have great deals all winter long, so it’s easy to catch one for a spontaneous visit.

caption:
HERE’S ALL YOU NEED TO KNOW ⬇️

🐢 Go early (8–8:30am) to enjoy it with fewer crowds
🐢 Skip regular sunscreen — wear UV-protective clothing to help protect the reef
🐢 Book a knowledgeable local guide who prioritizes wildlife respect and conservation
🐢 Use “Tortuga Loca - Crazy Turtle” parking right in front of the Tsuuk Akumal entrance
🐢 Leave your belongings in a locker before the tour
🐢 Tours last about 1 hour — if you have a hydrasuit, bring it! The mix of cenotes and ocean currents can make the water surprisingly cool

Because it’s a protected natural park, access is regulated and visitors must enter with an authorized guide.

After researching different options, we chose Ruben Torres @blueturtleakumal 
and had a great experience learning about the turtles and reef ecosystem.

🥗 Fun fact: turtles love this area because of the sea grass growing along the coast ☺️

📍 Tsuuk Akumal National Park (about 100km from Cancun)

🍽️ Nearby food spot we enjoyed: La Buena Vida — the fajitas, fried fish, and maracuya juice were amazing. There are also several restaurants right outside the entrance.

If you’re looking for a magical winter evening near Toronto — Winter Wonders at Royal Botanical Gardens (Burlington) @rbgcanada is the perfect pick.

Here’s what to know 👇🏼
✨ Dates: Open until January 4th, 2026
💰 Tickets: Available on the RBG website (purchase ahead — weekends get busy!)
🧣 Tip: Dress warm — most of the route is outdoors

🌲 What to Expect:
	•	A sparkling outdoor trail filled with glowing light installations, music, and holiday magic
	•	Indoor botanical garden sections to explore and warm up in between
	•	A miniature train town — dozens of tiny trains weaving through plants & landscapes (a favorite for kids and adults!)
	•	The charming Artisan Village — 6 cozy huts where local vendors sell handcrafted gifts & festive treats
	•	A family-friendly vibe with kids sliding in the snow and families soaking in the holiday spirit

It’s one of those places that makes you feel like you’ve stepped into a glowing storybook ✨

📍 Location: Royal Botanical Gardens, Burlington, ON
🎟️ Tickets: rbg.ca￼

caption:
❄️ WHO’S TUBING WITH YOU? 😎

But first — follow @across_continentss for more winter adventures, cozy date ideas, and hidden gems across Ontario! 🤍

If you’re not into skiing but still want to enjoy the slopes — snow tubing is your go-to winter thrill. Fast, easy, and absolutely hilarious (especially when you go down as a group 😅).

Here are the best tubing hills near Toronto 👇🏼

🛟 Snow Valley (Barrie) — One of the biggest tubing parks in Ontario! 14 chutes, 10-storey high, and a magic carpet lift back to the top.
🎟️ Tickets: from ~$35, book online early (they sell out fast!).

🛟 Lakeridge Resort (Uxbridge) — Closer to the city and great for families or beginners. They have 5 tubing lanes and warming areas to grab hot chocolate after.

🛟 Horseshoe Resort (Barrie) — Huge tubing hill with night lights and music — feels like a winter festival. You can also bundle it with spa access or dining for the perfect weekend getaway.

🛟 Chicopee Tube Park (Kitchener) TEMPORARILY CLOSED — A bit of a drive, but super organized with fast lanes and great staff. Bonus: an indoor lounge to warm up between rides.

💡 Tips before you go:
• Dress in layers and bring waterproof gloves 🧤
• Book online (especially weekends)
• Bring a stick/tripod to attach to your phone/camera
• Night tubing must be fun with lights & music (we haven’t tried though)

It’s honestly one of the easiest and most fun things to do in Toronto this winter — no skills needed, just laughter and snow! ☃️

caption:
YOUR GUIDE TO MAXIMIZING PTO 🧳✨

Before we share more about those places -  follow @across_continentss for more couple adventures, hidden gems, and travel inspo from Canada & beyond 🤍

📈How to travel more and spend less PTO:
- Plan the travel around a national holiday, like: Canada Day (Monday) and take Fri + Tue and Wed off.
- Plan early and find flights to include 2 weekends (so you need only 5 days off). With proper planning 9 days is decent for a trip.
- Remote work is a savior. It provides a lot of flexibility to explore after 5pm (or in the morning if you can shift hours)
- Network: Make friends around the world. We stayed at Alex’s friend apartments for up to a week in Montreal and spent evenings + weekends exploring 

5 Trips = 10 Places

🗺️ Banff - it was an amazing trip where we explored most of Canadian Rockies iconic places in 6 days.
🧮We managed to SPEND ONLY 3 VACATION DAYS there
Btw, we did tons of research on Banff, let us know in comments or DMs if you’d like to know more ☺️

🗺️ Calgary Stampede - the city is calm overall, but this festival brings so much life to the place. Rodeos are WILD 🐂

🗺️ Milano - spent 2 days out there and loved the architecture and the food scene. 

🗺️ Lake Como - the most aesthetic, peaceful and graceful location of our year 😍 (we don’t rate it over Banff, they’re just very different to compare). 

🗺️ Swiss Alps - we took the famous Bernina Express train from Italian Tirano to Swiss St Moritz. Worth every cent 🤩

🧮For Italy trip we took 5 vacation days, but made the most of the weekends and Victoria Day, so it became 10 days of our time there.

🗺️ Puerto Plata - colorful historical place on the North of the Dominican Republic.

🗺️ Cayo Arena - DR is a paradise island, and Cayo Arena is another incredible island inside the island😅

🗺️ Montreal - modern French vibe inside Canada. After Toronto feels like a relief - more style, less rush.

🗺️ British Columbia - except from exploring Banff, we couldn’t skip Yoho National park (and Emerald Lake)

🗺️ Canmore - are base in Canadian Rockies. More affordable than Banff, same insane views, gorgeous locations nearby (video is from Grassi Lakes)

But first, follow @across_continentss for more useful info about traveling in the Caribbean🔥

Before we dive in — save this for your next trip and comment “SALSA” for a full guide 🇲🇽
Here are some mistakes we’ve seen (or made) while exploring the Yucatán Peninsula 👇

📍 Skipping the cenotes
The Yucatán Peninsula is home to 6,000+ cenotes, some of the most unique natural pools in the world. These crystal-clear water formations are usually found in caves surrounded by limestone rock.

📍 Missing SFER IK (Uh May) Museum
This surreal art museum near Tulum is known for its organic architecture and immersive spaces. Even if you’re not into art, the building itself is worth the stop.

📍 Not swimming with turtles in Akumal
Akumal is one of the best places to see sea turtles in their natural habitat. With a guide, you can safely snorkel alongside them.

📍 Only using taxis in Tulum
Taxis can get very expensive. Renting bikes is a much better option and costs around 250 pesos per day, making it easy to explore the hotel zone.

📍 Skipping local beaches
Public beaches like Playa Delfines in Cancun are stunning and completely free. Some say it’s one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico. The other free beaches will be listed in our Mexico guide, so COMMENT OR DM “SALSA” to be the first one to get it☺️

📍 Using sunscreen at cenotes
Most sunscreens contain chemicals that ruin cenotes, corals and microorganisms living there. It’s best to find biodegradable ones to keep cenotes clear and always take a shower before getting in one.

📍 Not carrying cash
Many places like cenotes, parking areas, and small food stands still operate cash only, so having pesos with you is important.

caption:
🏞️ YOU WON’T FORGIVE YOURSELF IF YOU MISS THESE IN THE ROCKIES

Comment “PEAK” and we’ll send you our free Canadian Rockies map 📍

Before we dive in, follow @across_continentss for more Canada travel ideas ✈️

Save this for your Rockies trip

🏔️ Moraine Lake is the one you’ve seen everywhere and it really lives up to it, but you’ll need to book a shuttle in advance since cars aren’t allowed (SEE OUR DAY 2 for the details), and the Rockpile Trail is a super short walk for that iconic view

🌊 Lake Louise is just as impressive and if you’re up for it, the Lake Agnes Tea House hike and the Beehive hikes are 100% worth the effort

🐺 Peyto Lake is a quick stop with a short walk to the viewpoint and that unreal blue color, plus the shape actually looks like a wolf from above

🌿 Emerald Lake is in Yoho National Park and feels a bit more relaxed, perfect for slowing down, walking around, or just spending a few hours by the water.

There were lots of mosquitoes when we visited, bring the repellent!!!

💧 Grassi Lakes is an easy hike with forest views and bright turquoise lakes at the end, one of the most rewarding short trails

🏞️ Bow Lake is right off the road and makes for a perfect quick stop with mountain reflections and that classic Rockies view

🌅 Vermilion Lakes is such a peaceful spot, especially around sunrise or sunset with views of Mount Rundle

You can bring your pedal board to any lake, so do it if you’ve got an opportunity 🏄‍♂️

There are so many lakes in the Rockies, but these are the ones we’d go back to anytime

💬 Comment “COCO” to get a quiz and a 15% discount at the end of it our 90-page Dominican Republic travel guide, packed with locations, tips & hidden gems we found along the way!

We’ve spent weeks exploring the Dominican Republic — and it’s safe to say, it stole our hearts.
From mountain lunches to private islands, this is what your dream Caribbean trip could look like 👇🏼

📍 Cayo Arena
We woke up at 7 AM, took the boat at 8 AM, and had the entire island to ourselves. Just turquoise water, white sand, and silence. Pure paradise.

📍 27 Waterfalls of Damajagua
Sliding down waterfalls, hiking through the jungle — easily one of the most thrilling experiences we’ve ever had.

📍 Puerto Plata
Rented a retro car, explored colonial streets, and soaked in all the history. It felt like driving straight into the past.

📍 Piscina Natural (Rio San Juan)
We didn’t rent a yacht this time, but swam in the natural pool you see in the photo — and it was magical.
There’s a tricky path that leads there, but don’t worry — all the details are in our guide.

📍 El Molino de la Cumbre (near Santiago, San Víctor village)
A true hidden gem in the mountains! Peaceful, cozy, and serving incredible local dishes with jaw-dropping views.

✨ And there’s so much more:
– Swim under a tropical waterfall

We explored Puerto Plata for 3 days and loved how colorful, cultural, and adventurous this city is.

caption:
CAN’T BELIEVE THERE IS A DEAD LAND NEAR TORONTO😍🍂

But first, follow @across_continentss for more adventures in Ontario🥰

COMMENT “LEAF” for the FREE Ontario Fall Map 🗺️ 

We finally made it to the Cheltenham Badlands, and honestly — it’s even more surreal in person. Those rolling red hills look like something straight out of another planet, especially now when the fall colors are at their absolute peak. 🔥

It’s one of those spots that photos never fully capture — the contrast between the rusty red landscape and the golden trees around it is unreal. If you’ve been thinking about going, now’s 100% the time.

📍 Location: Cheltenham Badlands, Caledon, Ontario
🍁 Best time to visit: Right now — peak fall colors are at their best!
🎟️ Admission: Reservation required — $20 per vehicle for a 90-minute time slot (includes parking and access)
🚗 Distance from Toronto: About 1 hour drive
⚠️ Tips:
• Stay on designated boardwalks — walking directly on the hills isn’t allowed to help preserve them.
• Drones are not permitted anywhere on-site.
• You can book your time slot through the Credit Valley Conservation website before visiting.

This is why Badlands look so unique — the red hills were shaped over hundreds of years as wind and rain slowly eroded the soft clay soil. The rich color comes from iron in the ground that’s turned rusty over time. It’s one of those rare places in Ontario that looks stunning year-round, but in fall, it honestly feels like it’s glowing. 🌅

The trail follows the shoreline of Fairy Lake and takes you through forested sections, floating boardwalk, and beautiful viewpoints over the water.

It’s around 4.6 km one way (about 9 km round trip) - but there’s also an option to just see the boardwalk.

🚗 Distance from Toronto: ~2.5 hours drive

🕓 Trail length: 4.6 km one way

🍂 Best season: Fall, but beautiful year-round

💡 Tip: Go early morning for misty lake views and soft light for photos.

caption:
TORONTO’S SPOOKIEST STREET IS BACK 👻

I was just casually biking to my dance class when I turned onto Russell Hill Road and got freaked out for a second — there were ghosts, skeletons, and giant spiders everywhere. 😅

Turns out, this neighborhood takes Halloween decorating to another level. Almost every house was covered in cobwebs, creepy statues, and glowing pumpkins. Some even had fog machines and sound effects echoing through the street — it honestly felt like a movie set.

We’ve seen a lot of festive streets in Toronto, but Russell Hill Road always goes above and beyond this time of year. It’s become one of our favorite places to bike or walk in October — the decorations, the cozy atmosphere, and the fall leaves make it such a fun experience.

📍 Location: Russell Hill Rd, Forest Hill, Toronto
🕯️ Best time to visit: Just before sunset or early evening when the lights turn on
🚲 Tip: If you bike there, ride slowly — you’ll want to stop every few meters for photos!

YOU WON’T BELIEVE THIS VIEW IS JUST 45 MINUTES FROM TORONTO 😎

🍂 Just 45 minutes from Toronto, Rattlesnake Point Conservation Area is one of those Ontario hikes that instantly makes you forget you’re near the city. Towering cliffs, golden forests, and sweeping views of the escarpment — it’s pure fall magic.

🥾 The trails range from easy to moderate, so whether you’re looking for a chill stroll or a mini workout, there’s a route for you. The Buffalo Crag Trail (3 km) is our favorite — it leads you straight to some of the best lookout points in Halton.

📸 Sunrise and sunset here are next-level beautiful, especially in October when the leaves go full fire mode. Bring your camera — and maybe a thermos of something warm.

🧗‍♀️ Fun fact: the area is also popular with rock climbers! You’ll often see them scaling the cliffs while you’re enjoying the views from above.

Good to know:
🎟️ Reservation required
(book through Conservation Halton’s website)

💵 Entry fee applies (included with reservation)

🚗 ~45 minutes from Toronto

caption:
HURRY UP, FALL COLORS ARE AT THEIR PEAK 😇

🍂 One of our favorite fall viewpoints in Ontario — Dundas Peak Lookout — never disappoints. If you’re chasing those golden-red leaves and dramatic cliff views, this spot should be at the top of your list!

🎒 The hike isn’t too long (around 3.5 km round trip) but it does get your heart rate up — totally worth it once you reach the edge and see Hamilton and the valley spread out below.

📸 Pro tip: go early morning or just before sunset for the best lighting (and fewer crowds). Bring a thermos of coffee, sit on the rocks, and just take it all in.

🍁 Fun fact: Dundas Peak is part of the Spencer Gorge Conservation Area, which also includes Webster’s and Tew’s Falls — so you can turn it into a full-day adventure.

caption:
WE MADE MISTAKE # 7 WAY TOO MANY TIMES🫠

🧥Before we dive into the details, most of the hikes this fall we did in jackets from @aparso_canada. They’re super light, colorful, sustainable, and made from high-quality recyclable materials — perfect for fall photos and layering on windy days.

Comment “Aparso” to get a DISCOUNT CODE on Aparso clothing 😍

Here’re 15 common mistakes people make and how to avoid them 👇🏼

🚫 1️⃣ Not checking weather or fall foliage reports – The colors and trail conditions change fast — always check the park’s live updates before heading out.

💧 2️⃣ Bringing too much or too little water – Hydration is key, but overpacking water adds unnecessary weight. Aim for 0.5L per hour of hiking.

⏰ 3️⃣ Arriving outside your reserved time slot – Many parks now have strict entry windows. We were turned around when we got a bit late for the Grotto hike on the Bruce Peninsula. The more popular the area is - the stricter the rules!

🧥 4️⃣ Not wearing proper layers – Fall weather can flip from warm to freezing. Layers are your best friend.

🔥 5️⃣ Cooking or storing food too close to tents – It attracts wildlife (especially raccoons and bears). Keep your food away and sealed.

📱 6️⃣ Not downloading offline maps – Cell service can disappear quickly — download maps ahead of time in AllTrails or Google Maps offline mode.

🎟️ 7️⃣ Not booking reservations early enough – Popular parks like Algonquin and Sandbanks fill up weeks in advance, especially in fall. When we tried to secure lodging or even access to some Algonquin trails in the beginning of October - they were already booked 🫣

🦟 8️⃣ Skipping mosquito or tick protection – they’re always around.

caption:
🍁DON’T MISS THESE 20 SPOTS IN TORONTO TO CATCH GOLDEN FALL COLORS! (ACCESSIBLE BY TTC)🚇

You don’t need a car to enjoy Toronto’s autumn magic — the city is full of cozy parks, colorful trails, and charming neighborhoods you can reach right by TTC.
♥️Follow @across_continentss for wild adventures & hidden gems in Toronto! 🍁

 Here are our favorite places to soak up the fall vibes 👇🏼
🍂 1️⃣ Cedarvale Ravine Stairs – Hidden under the bridge in Centrevale Park, surrounded by golden trees and quiet trails. Such a peaceful little pocket of nature.
🍁 2️⃣ Prince Charles Park – A small park with plenty of charm — we love stopping here for a fall picnic under its bright red trees.
🌳 3️⃣ Sunnybrook Park – One of our go-to weekend spots. Huge open fields, winding trails, and picnic areas that come alive in autumn colors.
🌅 4️⃣ Palace Pier Park – Grab takeout and enjoy the skyline by Humber Bay Bridge — it’s such a cozy waterfront view.
🚴‍♀️ 5️⃣ Edwards Gardens – Perfect for biking or long walks. The trails and vibrant foliage make it feel like a movie set this time of year.
🏛️ 6️⃣ Emanuel College (U of T) – Historic architecture meets fall beauty. We love walking here — the contrast of ivy-covered walls and orange trees is just stunning.
🏘️ 7️⃣ Summerhill – A dreamy walk from Summerhill to Rosedale Station, full of markets, cafés, and houses decorated for fall.
🚴‍♂️ 8️⃣ Forest Hill & Russell Hill Road – One of the most scenic biking routes in Toronto, lined with colorful trees and beautiful homes.
🏙️ 9️⃣ Don Mills Area – This neighborhood really leans into the season — cozy cafés, outdoor shopping squares, and fall decorations everywhere.
🌲 1️⃣0️⃣ Glendon Forest (York University) – We love biking here. The winding path through the woods feels like a mini getaway inside the city.

caption:
🌊 WHO’S COMING WITH YOU TO NF NEXT TIME?

✨ Before we dive in, don’t forget to follow @across_continentss for world travels and useful tips!

📍 Niagara Falls isn’t just about standing at the viewpoint — here’s what you should actually do 👇

💧 Tunnel to Niagara Falls – Included with Power Station ticket. Walk through a long tunnel to a platform right at the base of Horseshoe Falls.

💧 White Water Walk – $19.55. A short boardwalk right by Class 6 rapids. Super powerful to see up close.

💧 Whirlpool Jet – Around $70+ and pure adrenaline. A fast ride through the rapids that’s unforgettable.

💧 Skylon Tower – $16. Observation deck with panoramic views of the Falls and city.

💧 Whirlpool Aero Car – $19. A suspended cable car that glides over the Niagara Whirlpool — a quick but thrilling ride with incredible views.

💧 Niagara Parks Power Station – $28. A historic building where you learn how Niagara’s water was turned into electricity.

❄️ Frozen Falls in Winter – Free. Seeing the Falls surrounded by ice and mist is like another world.

💧 Journey Behind the Falls – $23.50. Tunnels that take you behind the waterfall itself. Loud, wet, and unforgettable.

💧 Niagara Falls Cruise – $43 and worth every penny. You’ll get soaked and the view from below is insane.

💧 Falls Incline Railway – $2.66 one way. A simple but fun ride that saves you the steep walk up.

💧 Niagara Falls Botanical Garden – Free. A calm escape with seasonal flowers and greenery.

💧 Falls at Night – Free. The Falls lit up in colors every evening, plus fireworks on weekends.

❄️ Frozen Falls in Winter – Free. Seeing the Falls surrounded by ice and mist is like another world.

caption:
SAVE THIS IF YOU WANT TO SEE THE NORTHERN LIGHTS IN CANADA 🌌

🤩 Finally seeing aurora is the feeling that’s hard to describe, “unreal” is the closest. 
What made it even more special is that we caught it near Barrie, Ontario, just a short drive from Toronto. 

😇 You don’t always need to travel far north; sometimes, all it takes is going up to a place with clear, dark sky (check Dark Sky Map for that) and a bit of patience. ✨

💫 2026 is expected to be the best year in a decade to see the Northern Lights, thanks to increased solar activity. If you’ve ever wanted to witness them, now’s the time to plan your trip.

👉 Best Places to See Them in Canada are listed on Slide 3 — but if you’re in Ontario, you can still get lucky on clear nights. Find an open area away from city lights and set up alerts on an aurora app so you don’t miss the moment.

📅 Best months: November – March
🕙 Best hours: 10 PM – 2 AM
🌕 Choose clear, moonless nights for the brightest colors.

For the most magical experience:
 🧣 Dress warm,  really warm.
 ☕ Bring a thermos of hot tea or cocoa.
 💫 Be patient - the most breathtaking moments often come after hours of waiting.

caption:
🌟Comment “GEM” to get a freebie! 🌟

Our freebie contains 10 most Instagram-worthy places in Quebec City, some are not on this list😍

Here’s the full list of places that you can SAVE:

🏰 Fairmont Le Château Frontenac – The most photographed hotel in the world, right in Old Quebec.

🥘 La Bûche – Traditional Québécois food with hearty portions (poutine, tourtière, maple desserts).

🚶‍♀️ Downtown Streets of Old Quebec – Cobblestone alleys, boutiques, and European vibes.

🎆 Waterfront Fireworks – Stunning shows along the St. Lawrence, especially in summer.

🌊 Montmorency Falls – Higher than Niagara! Take the cable car, zipline, or suspension bridge.

🌲 Beaupré – Scenic village just outside Quebec City, gateway to outdoor adventures.

🏛 City Hall – Gorgeous architecture and photo spot, especially in the evening.

🌳 Domaine de Maizerets – Beautiful park with gardens, trails, and a historic manor.

💦 Chute Jean Larose – A hidden waterfall near Mont-Sainte-Anne with 400+ steps to reach it.

✨ Onhwa’ Lumina – Immersive night walk telling Indigenous stories through lights and sound.

🛡 Parc du Bastion de la Reine – Panoramic viewpoint over Old Quebec’s walls.

🌄 Canyon Sainte-Anne – Dramatic canyon with suspension bridges and hiking trails.

🏛 Parliament Building – Free tours inside Quebec’s impressive National Assembly.

🪶 Huron-Wendat Traditional Site (Wendake) – Learn Indigenous history, try traditional meals, explore the longhouse.

🌬 Parc des Moulins (Windmills Park) – Peaceful escape with old stone windmills and wide trails.

💡 TIP: Most of these are within Quebec City, but Montmorency Falls, Canyon Sainte-Anne, and Wendake are quick day trips. Plan 3–4 days for the full experience.

🏔️Here’s all you need to know:

Where to Kayak in Banff National Park:

1️⃣ Moraine Lake — Iconic, surreal blue water (canoe rentals only, but you can bring your own paddleboard)

2️⃣ Lake Louise — Stunning backdrop of glaciers (canoe rentals only, but private paddleboards are allowed)

3️⃣ Two Jack Lake — Calm, beginner-friendly, perfect for kayaking & SUP (own equipment allowed)

4️⃣ Johnson Lake — Warmest lake in Banff, great for relaxing paddles (own equipment allowed)

5️⃣ Vermilion Lakes — Close to Banff town, beautiful for sunrise or sunset (own equipment allowed)

💵 Rentals & Prices (Summer 2025):
• Canoe rentals at Moraine Lake and Lake Louise — $160 CAD per hour (+tax)
• Kayak and SUP rentals — available in Banff town, $40–$80 CAD per day depending on duration and type
• Personal paddleboards/kayaks — allowed on all lakes, but parking/shuttle rules apply at Moraine & Louise

🚌 Access & Parking:
• Moraine Lake — Shuttle required ($8 CAD per person). No private cars.
• Lake Louise — Paid parking $36 CAD/day or shuttle
• All other lakes — Have parking lots, first-come, first-served

💡 Tip
Bring layers — water is freezing even in summer

caption:
SO MANY GEMS IN ONE TOWN! 🍂⬇️

✈️ Follow @across_continentss for more Ontario getaways, cozy towns, and fall adventures!

Drive 2 hours from Toronto to discover the charm of 📍Stratford, the WINNER in our “Cute Towns” series!

🍫 Start your day with the Chocolate or Bacon Trail -  a fun way to explore the town while tasting treats from local vendors.

🚶‍♂️ Join a walking food tour with Lauri @stratford_walking_tours where she’ll tell you all about Stratford’s history along with stopping in delicious lunch spots.

🚤 Rent a kayak at @avonboathouse and take a peaceful ride on Lake Victoria - very romantic and calming experience ❣️

🎶 Justin Bieber’s fans, run, don’t walk to the Perth Museum @stratfordperthmuseum to experience probably his biggest exhibit (which he actually visited)! 
As Stratford is his hometown, the staff will tell you stories you’ve never heard of him and show his personal items (check out those tank tops we tried on!).

🎨 For art lovers, don’t miss the Stratford Art Gallery @gallerystratford . It’s home to a collection of inspiring exhibitions featuring Canadian artists and creative works.

🍽️ Dine at the Revival House @revivalhouse_on , a unique restaurant set inside a historic church. We don’t know about you, but that’s the first time we heard of such a thing! (btw the food was so mouthwatering!)

🎬 End your day with a private film screening at the Guinness Award winning world’s smallest cinema @thelittleprincecinema , also known for its irresistible popcorn and creative decorations. One more gem: they have lots of old candies that you won’t find in stores anymore!

🏠We recommend staying overnight not to rush and to enjoy everything Stratford has to offer.For a one-of-a-kind accommodation, check out @fivestratford , perfect for making your stay extra special.

caption:
A Classy Escape to the 19th Century 🌸✨

This town is our go-to spot for a romantic getaway! 
Follow us for more towns like this @across_continentss 

😻 Fun fact: July 20th marked our 3-year anniversary of living in Canada, and Niagara-on-the-Lake was our first home after arriving here! We were lucky enough to find a local host, who gave us shelter for the first few weeks. We had a wonderful opportunity to stay there and explore every corner!

🫶🏼 We also thought all Bridgerton fans would love to visit this magical place!

Here’s the first list of must-do’s in Niagara-on-the-Lake:

🌺 Visit Prince of Wales Hotel: Built in 1864, this historic hotel is a perfect backdrop for your Bridgerton-inspired photoshoot. It is free to enter and explore the interior of the building! They also have traditional afternoon tea ceremonies, so make sure to book one!

🍝 Dine at Shaw Cafe + Wine Bar: Enjoy a delightful meal and fine wine, just like the high society gatherings in Bridgerton! We loved sitting on a terrace next to the George Bernard Shaw statue and contemplating life. 🍷

🧪 Visit Niagara Apothecary: This free museum amazed us with its selection of different bottles, jars, and flasks frozen in time and accurately placed on the shelves! We stayed there for a good half an hour, imagining our life in the 19th century. It is crazy to think it operated from 1820 to 1964!

🍦 Enjoy ice cream at COWS: When you enter the store, you smell freshly made cones and want to try every possible flavor right away, haha😅. They also have a selection of fun cow-print goodies.

🥰 Explore cute shops on Queen Street: It’s a great idea to stroll around and drop into each little spot!

🚣‍♀️ Elora Gorge Tubing
Until September 2 - every day
Until September 30 - only weekends

scroll 2 reels down to our other reel for all info and more visuals
Cost: $10.50 admission (reservation required) + $35 tubing package (tube, helmet, life jacket)

No need to buy your own tube if you don’t have one!

Bring: water shoes, waterproof phone case with strap, sunscreen

Parking fills fast, arrive early! The 2 km ride has light rapids and takes 1–2 hours. you need to walk back with your tube for another run.

🏊‍♂️ Elora Quarry – a former limestone quarry turned swimming hole with cliffs and turquoise water. open daily in summer until labour day.
cost: $10.50 admission

limited capacity, book online IN ADVANCE
bring: water shoes, sunscreen, snacks (no alcohol or glass)

🏛 Wellington county museum & archives – located between elora and fergus, housed in a former poorhouse. Admission is $10

SAVE FOR YOUR ROCKIES TRIP PLANNING 🗺️

Banff and Jasper National Parks have a ton of gorgeous lakes, but these are the most stunning in our opinion:

1. Moraine Lake 🏔️
• Only accessible by shuttle (mid-June to mid-Oct) — no private cars
• Best at sunrise — unreal colors and reflections
• Bring layers — it gets chilly early morning
• Reserve your shuttle in advance (especially for sunrise slots)

2. Lake Louise 🛶
• 40$ parking at Lake Louise parking lot or use Parks Canada shuttle
• Easy lakeside trail or hike to Lake Agnes Tea House
• Canoe rental available, but pricey (~$145/hour for 2 ppl)
• Very popular — go early to avoid crowds

3. Peyto Lake 🐺
• 10-min walk from parking lot to main viewpoint
• Often crowded — go early or late in the day
• Hidden viewpoint ~300m past main platform (quieter and better)
• No shuttle needed

4. Emerald Lake 💚
• Located in Yoho National Park (~30 min from Lake Louise)
• Walk the flat trail around the lake (~5 km)
• Canoe rentals available (cheaper and calmer than Louise)
• Beautiful in all weather — even on cloudy days

5. Grassi Lakes 🥾
• Located in Canmore — great short hike option
• Choose between easy trail or scenic waterfall route
• Crystal-clear turquoise water
• Popular with locals — great mid-morning stop

caption:
DETAILS OF MORAINE LAKE TRIP ⬇️🌄
Here’s how to plan the perfect visit (with prices!)

🚐 Getting There
- You can’t drive to Moraine Lake — book the Alpine Start Shuttle in advance (tickets sell out months ahead). 
- Check out Parks Canada website!
- We booked the earliest 4 AM departure (called Alpine start) and paid $40 for car parking. 
- If you are taking a later Moraine Lake Shuttle - you’d need to use the other parking lot, just read your confirmation very thoroughly.
- No service at the parking lot — download maps & screenshot your confirmation.
- The driver will give you purple return tickets for a shuttle back.

🥶 What to Expect
• It’s cold before sunrise — wear warm layers
• Bring a thermos, head lamp and snacks — you’ll be waiting ~1 hr before the sun rises
• Views are totally worth it — quiet trails, peaceful moments, and canoe views

🛶 Things to Do
• Walk the lakeside trail
• Rent a canoe for $160 + tax/hour (no shorter option) or bring your own paddleboard
• There’s also a lodge + restaurant if you want to stay overnight (sells out way in advance)

• Tickets: $25 adults | $7 under 25 | Free for kids under 6.

💡 Tips for Visiting
• Plan 2–3 hours for the gallery + grounds.
• Wear comfy shoes for trails.
• Grab a blanket and have a picnic there!
• Check the gallery website for temporary exhibitions and free admission days.

✨ Tubing at Elora Gorge is one of the most exciting summer adventures we’ve done in Ontario so far — sliding down the rapids was WILD 😝 

🌊 Here’s the Complete Guide to tubing there!

📍 Location
• Just 1.5 hours from Toronto in Elora, Ontario
• A 2 km tubing ride through limestone cliffs and rapids on the Grand River

⏳ Season & Hours
• Open daily June 25 – Labour Day (September 30)
• Weekends only until September 30 (weather permitting)
• Rentals close at 4 PM, equipment must be returned by 7 PM

🎟 Tickets & Pricing
• Online booking required (day-use passes often sell out)
• Park entry: $9/adult
• Tubing package: $54/person (tube, helmet, life jacket included)
• Refundable deposit: $75 per rental

🚗 Parking & Logistics
• Large parking lot inside Elora Gorge Conservation Area
• 1.3 km walk between launch point & exit (each way)
• No lifeguards on site - the river is just too long, so don’t take off the vest

🎒 What to Bring
• Closed-toe water shoes or running shoes with grip
• Waterproof phone case + strap (phones often get lost!)
• Sunglasses with strap, sunscreen, water, snacks
• Towel & change of clothes

🛟 Equipment
• No need to bring your own tube — rentals cover everything you need
• Helmets & lifejackets are mandatory (provided with rental)

Banff is beautiful but overpriced and always packed. Canmore is calmer, cheaper, and only 20 min away.

Parks Canada tickets sell out in minutes — line up online with multiple devices on release day.

ALL DETAILS OF DAY 3 PART 2 ⬇️🥾

Here’s how to plan the Little Beehive hike after a Moraine Lake sunrise with real tips!

🥱 Starting the Day
If you’re doing an Alpine Start at Moraine Lake, expect to wake up around 2 AM and stay active until evening.
We were exhausted, so hiking Little Beehive after sunrise was a true challenge.

🥗 Quick Breakfast Stop
The only somewhat affordable meal in Banff is at Fairmont Lake Louise.
We grabbed a pre‑made salad with chicken, eggs, kale, tomatoes, avocado, corn & gorgonzola — surprisingly yummy!
Tip: public washrooms are only at the parking lot (Fairmont ones are locked for guests).

🥾 Trail Details
• Lake Agnes Tea House – 3.5 km one way (steady forest climb)
• Big Beehive – +1.5 km from tea house
• Little Beehive – +800 m from tea house (easier option)
• Pass Mirror Lake & small waterfalls along the way
• Tea House offers snacks & drinks with stunning views

📝 Our Hiking Tips
• Pack light – elevation gain feels easier
• Bring 3 bottles of water, mosquito spray & snacks
• Wear proper hiking shoes – trails can be rocky & slippery
• Horseback rides are available – but we don’t recommend as horses struggle on the steep paths
• For crowd‑free photos at Lake Louise – step on shallow lake rocks if your shoes allow.

caption:
DON’T VISIT MORAINE LAKE WITHOUT THESE TIPS🥹🏞️

📍Location
Moraine Lake, Alberta (Banff National Park)

Before we dive in, if you’re planning your trip to Banff, follow @across_continentss for our Rockies adventures! We have a lot to share 🥰

✏️ How to get there:
Parks Canada offers shuttles for only $8, but you have to book them at the very beginning of the season.
This season, they released booking slots in early April—and everything sold out within the first hour.
If you don’t catch the government shuttle, private shuttles cost from $60 CAD per person.

‼️ YOU CAN’T DRIVE THERE ON YOUR OWN WITHOUT A SHUTTLE

😴 The earliest shuttle time is 4 AM—the alpine start.
For that, you have to park your car at the Lake Louise parking lot ($36 🫠), and then take the booked shuttle to Moraine Lake.

🛶 Canoe Rentals (in summer 2025):
1 hour = $160 + tax
Note: you can bring your own paddle board if you want/can

What to bring:
Hot tea
Blanket
Layers
Warm hat
Snacks/breakfast

DO WE REGRET WAKING UP THAT EARLY?
Absolutely not—it was stunning! The best way to start the day ⭐️

But be smarter than us and don’t plan anything intense afterward.
We stayed in a hostel in Canmore and had only 3 hours of sleep, which felt exhausting on a day full of hiking.

We hope this helps and that you have an excellent time at Moraine Lake 😇

caption:
DO NOT FALL FOR THE LAST ONE ⬇️ 

1. Not checking ferry schedules thoroughly. If you miss one, the next one might be only in a few hours.

2. Choosing Varenna as a base. Varenna is a gorgeous little town, but it has 0 grocery stores. Menaggio or Bellagio seems way better for a couple days stay.

3. Booking villas in advance in low season. Rain can come unexpectedly, and you don’t want to be forced to go at that time. Crowds weren’t too bad in mid-May, so we only booked Villa Balbianello as it’s the most popular one.

4. Not buying a ticket for Villa del Balbianello on grandigiardini. This website sells tickets for all villas, and seems to have tickets available, even when Villa del Balbianello is sold out on their website. 
We know, it sounds weird, but it’s legit.

Follow us @across_continentss for more mindblowing content from gorgeous Italy! 🇮🇹 

5. Not running to Villa Cipressi gates in the morning. This is probably the most famous gates in Lake Como where everyone wants a picture. 
Don’t judge, but we waited an hour to film a few videos 😢

6. Being upset if the weather forecast shows the whole day of rain. Mostly like it’s gonna be half day max, so don’t bother.

7. Drinking more Aperol Spritz instead of wine. We love Aperol, but a bottle of wine in a store starts from €3, so why not to take advantage?😅

8. 🚤 Not renting a boat. Renting a boat for a day, checking out different towns at your own pace and just hanging out on the sun is one of the best things you can experience in Lake Como area. Still in our bucket list for the next time.

9. Not pre-downloading maps. Connection is poor sometimes, so better to have them loaded.

10. Forgetting an umbrella/raincoat. It’s one of the wettest regions in Italy, so there’s a high chance you’ll get some rain even in the summer😅

caption:
ALL YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT THIS GEM 🥾💎

This short hike near Canmore is one of the best easy trails in the Canadian Rockies:
💙 turquoise water
🌲 forest views
💦 waterfall vibes in just over an hour!

Here’s everything you need to know before you go:

📍Location
• Grassi Lakes Trail is in Canmore, Alberta, about 1 hour from Banff and just 5 minutes from downtown Canmore.
• A great day trip if you’re based in Canmore or Banff.

🚗 Parking
• There’s a free Grassi Lakes Day Use parking lot at the trailhead.
• It fills up fast on weekends — arrive early or late afternoon for easier parking.
⚠️ You need to pay for parking near Grassi Lakes as a Kananaskis Conservation Pass is required for parking in Kananaskis Country, where the trail is located.
It can be done online quickly.

🚌 Public Transportation
• Roam Transit Bus Route 12 - no parking stress 😉

🥾 Trail Info
• Length: ~4 km round trip (about 1 to 1.5 hours depending on your pace)
• Elevation Gain: ~250 m
• Two routes:
 – Easy route (gravel road) — good for families and casual walkers
 – Scenic route — steeper with stairs, forest views, and a waterfall (our pick!)
• Trail is well-marked and open year-round (icy in winter — bring spikes)

🎒 What to Bring
• Water & snacks
• Proper walking/hiking shoes (even the “easy” trail has a bit of incline)
• Bug spray (can be buggy in summer)
• Camera or phone — the lakes are incredibly photogenic
• Layers — weather can change fast

💭 In Case you Wondered
• Dogs allowed on leash
• No swimming in the lakes (it’s a conservation area)
• No trash bins on the trail — pack out what you bring
• No entrance or park fee

.☺️ Definitely worth the short hike and a perfect intro to the Rockies if you’re not into intense trails.

caption:
⬇️ SAVE NOT TO REPEAT OUR MISTAKES 📝

🇮🇹 We have just returned from a trip to Milan and Lake Como, and these scams (or sometimes just rules that tourists are not aware of) are really a thing there, so pay attention on your next trip to Italy:

1️⃣ “Free” bracelets
A person approaches and ties a bracelet on your wrist “as a gift,” then demands money and won’t leave until you pay.

2️⃣ Fake Petition. 
Often done by young people pretending to collect signatures for a charity or cause. While you’re distracted, an accomplice may pickpocket you. (Lots of other variations which bases on distracting the target)

3️⃣ Overpriced photos. 
Gladiators near the Colosseum or masked figures in Venice may offer a photo, then demand €10–€20+ after.

4️⃣ “Helpful” people offer to assist with your ticket machine or luggage, then demand a tip or steal your bags.

5️⃣ Rose or Gift Scam
A man offers you a flower or small trinket “as a gift” then aggressively demands payment when you take 

6️⃣ Paintings on the floor. 
Scammers put lots of paintings on the floor in the most inconvenient so people accidentally step on them. After people do step on them, they force them to pay for the caused “damage”.

7️⃣ English menu prices are higher than in the original menu.

8️⃣ Price of coffee/wine in Italy differs depending on whether you’re standing or sitting. If you decide to sit, you’ll be charged “coperto” - a cover charge. If you want to avoid cover charge - ask to have your coffee on the counter “al banco”.
“Coperto” is usually about 2-3€

‼️9 and 10 will be in the comments

Now you know how to protect your money, which means ready to enjoy everything Italy had to offer 🍝

If you’re near Niagara Falls this season, don’t skip the Centennial Lilac Garden — it’s like walking through a living bouquet.

Located right next to the Floral Clock, this garden is home to over 1,200 lilac bushes in 200+ varieties.

💫 The lilacs bloom around mid-May to early June, making it one of the most peaceful and underrated spring spots in the Niagara region.

🌿 It’s completely free to visit, has tons of space for a walk or picnic, and is perfect for couples, families, or solo explorers who love flowers and quiet views.

caption:
ALL YOU NEED TO KNOW ⬇️

📍 Location: Banff National Park, Alberta

⏰ Best time to visit: Early morning to avoid the crowds

💰 Cost: Included with your Parks Canada pass (or $11/person per day)

Johnston Canyon is one of the most popular hikes in Banff, and for good reason — two waterfalls, catwalks along the canyon, and even a chance to reach the Inkpots if you want to go further.

🏞 Lower Falls
• Features a small cave where you can peek at the waterfall up close
• Expect 20–30 min wait during peak hours for a photo at the cave
• Pretty, but not as jaw-dropping as the Upper Falls

🏞 Upper Falls
• The highlight of the hike — definitely worth the climb!
• Lines for the viewpoint can be just as long, so go early if you want a clean photo
• From here, you can continue to the Inkpots (around 3 km further) for colorful mineral pools in a peaceful valley

🔒 Secret Cave:
There’s a hidden cave along the trail, but it’s seasonally closed to protect nesting birds. Check local guidelines before planning to visit it.

🔥 Our Tip:
We skipped the Ink pots this time because we had no cell service and weren’t sure about the route, but if you’re ready for a longer hike, it’s a beautiful add-on.
